close_reason: The motivating seal runaway no longer exists, and a two-tier provisional-publication model would duplicate consistency ownership. fz-kdt.34 now owns the single generic concept: monotone current cells plus a quiescent group epoch for consumers requiring finality.
description:
The scheduler hard-couples "did this job finish with waits" to "extend vs replace
its outputs", so a job that publishes partial evidence while still waiting can
never mark that evidence provisional. Whether it SHOULD be able to is the
question.

## Premise verified at main 417c5b0b5

The partial-publication design exists and is documented at the site
(jobs/semantic.rs:212-214):

    // Waits no longer bail: a waiting completion extends the job's standing
    // claims (it cannot retract), so partial evidence publishes safely and
    // the waits simply ride the final effects.

and jobs/semantic.rs:244-245 still reads cone-peer `ReturnType` as a READ, not a
wait ("so mutual recursion cannot deadlock").

The coupling is at scheduler.rs:261-296:

    let waiting = !waits.is_empty();
    ... extend_outputs + mark_dirty   vs   replace_outputs

`grep -rn "provisional" src/` returns NOTHING, so the proposed two-tier
publication was never built.

Of the six retracting fact kinds it measured, `RuntimeDemand` is no longer a
`FactKey` at all (drive.rs:89-119) -- it is a pull product (pull.rs:43). The
other five survive: CallSiteSummary, Activation, ActivationAnalyzed, ReturnType,
Executable.

## THE MOTIVATION IS GONE

This was filed to cure a seal runaway. `SealSemanticClosure`,
`DeriveTransportPlan` and `DeriveRuntimeDemand` all grep to ZERO hits. The stated
target (`seal <= 32`) names nothing that exists, and the parent's gate test
`compiler2_enum_take_drop_split_seals_without_reseal_runaway` has been deleted.
`follow_up` survives only as three comment/test references naming it as a retired
anti-pattern.

So the DEADLOCK-SAFETY question is still real and still unanswered, but it is now
a question about the scheduler's publication model in the abstract, not a cure
for a specific runaway.

## Its measurements are unreproducible

~4040 re-publishes, ~395 retractions, ~14000 ascents came from a raw-event2
telemetry channel the CLI JSONL sink does not serialize. Only
`fz.compiler2.job`, `pull.product.settled`, `demand.cone.settled`,
`backend_program.defined`, `pull.session.finished`, `lexer.*` and `diag.*` appear
in the log. Re-measuring needs an in-process test, not the binary. Same
instrumentation gap as fz-kdt.41.

## What is measurable today

enum_take_drop_split, two runs, byte-identical: 2593 job spans, 12352
product.settled, AnalyzeActivation 1382. Wall clock 4.91/4.94/4.92s. Slow but
DETERMINISTIC -- which is the material change from when this was filed, and means
any churn here can be bisected rather than chased.

## Recommendation

Do not start this as a perf cure. Either close it, or restate it as a scheduler
design question -- "should a waiting job be able to publish provisional
evidence?" -- with a fresh motivation, since the runaway it was written for no
longer exists.

Line drift: semantic.rs:179 -> now lands in `merge_callsite_input_vec`;
the partial-publish site is jobs/semantic.rs:212; scheduler.rs:115/124/133 ->
scheduler.rs:269/278/287.
title: Deadlock-safe settled-gating of downstream-visible replacing facts: the scheduler cannot mark partial evidence provisional
